# Independent audit: exponential floor and retained logarithmic scale

Audited `candidate 942ae5a91bb1a792` in full, together with its stated hypotheses in `candidate 3432196fb93eb580`.

**PASS. No correction is needed.** The floor, joint rate measures, perspective convexity, both limit passages and the upper-tail inequality all follow under the displayed SAME physical-separator hypotheses. The note does not silently assert defect exclusion or a pointwise limiting cap selector bound.

## 1. Actual admissibility and the pointwise floor

For a fixed index j, positivity of the finite-PL concave L_j on the current compact canonical hull gives a slightly larger open convex neighborhood where it is positive. The functions used in the proof are finite convex on that neighborhood. On an intermediate compact convex neighborhood their subgradients are bounded; the supremum of the corresponding affine supports is globally finite and agrees on the original body. If an explicitly globally nonnegative test is desired, its positive part preserves that agreement. Uniformity of these slopes in j is neither used nor required, because the SAME separator admits every such test at each fixed j.

Writing a_j=beta_j/lambda_j+C, the positive part Phi=(ell_j-a_j)_+ is convex. On its support,

    Xi_j>=-beta_j+lambda_j ell_j-C lambda_j=lambda_j Phi.

Thus the separator gives zero integral of Phi squared. Boundary measure has full support on every positive convex fiber boundary, so continuity makes Phi zero everywhere on those boundaries. A concave function is at least the minimum of its boundary values at interior points; applying concavity again to the canonical sampled hull gives the asserted floor everywhere. This includes interval endpoints with counting boundary measure.

The max with zero in the rate bound is correct. In the cap application beta_j>=0, and the common rate interval is compact because beta_j converges and lambda_j tends to zero.

## 2. Joint weak limits and the quadratic reserve

The measures Bhat_j and Ahat_j have bounded masses, are carried by one compact space, and satisfy 0<=Ahat_j<=Bhat_j. On every compact set where L is bounded away from zero, logarithms converge uniformly and the recorded rate tends uniformly to zero. The bounded normal/selector weak limits therefore identify precisely the ordinary parts in (4).

The residuals are nonnegative restrictions to the zero set. The assumption eta({L=0})=0 is important here: it keeps ordinary and residual parts disjoint and gives 0<=ahat<=bhat after subtraction. It is present in the source.

Multiplication by the bounded continuous recorded coordinate r passes to the weak limit. Consequently the projection of r bhat is exactly the old quadratic reserve q. No extra uniform-integrability assumption for lambda_j ell_j squared is being slipped in; its control now follows from bounded rate times bounded logarithmic mass.

## 3. Convexity of the enlarged perspective family

For g finite, nonnegative, convex and nondecreasing, k(s)=s_+g(lambda s_+) is convex and nondecreasing. On the positive half-line its derivative is g(lambda s)+lambda s g'(lambda s), a nondecreasing nonnegative function. At zero its right derivative is g(0)>=0 and its left derivative is zero. These one-sided facts handle nonsmooth g directly.

Put K=k'+k''. For smooth pieces the Hessian of F(a,b)=a k(log(a/b)-T) is

    K * [[1/a, -1/b], [-1/b, a/b^2]],

which is positive semidefinite and has determinant zero. Equivalently, the perspective function phi(t)=t k(log t-T) has phi''=(k'+k'')/t>=0. Approximation on a slightly larger compact argument interval, or the distributional second derivative, proves the same statement across kinks. The monotonicities are F_a=k+k'>=0 and F_b=-(a/b)k'<=0.

Therefore composing the first argument with convex f and the second with concave L_j has the correct sign: at a convex combination, first increase the first argument to its affine average and decrease the second argument to its affine average, and then apply joint convexity. This verifies actual convexity of every test (6), rather than just of a formal scalar expression.

Every such g is Lipschitz on the relevant compact rate interval. In particular its behavior at zero causes no exception: convexity and nondecreasingness bound its nonnegative right slopes by a secant on a slightly larger finite interval.

## 4. Independent limit bookkeeping

For fixed positive f and fixed T, let s=ell_{j,+}, c=T-log f>0, and t=(s-c)_+. Then

    t g(lambda_j t)-s g(lambda_j s)+(s-t)g(0)
       =t[g(lambda_j t)-g(lambda_j s)]
          -(s-t)[g(lambda_j s)-g(0)].                (A)

Since s-t<=c, the absolute value in (A) is at most 2 Lip(g) lambda_j c s. Its boundary integral tends to zero. The bounded correction f min(s,c)g(0) is continuous as a function of (L_j,w), including L_j=0 after setting the truncated logarithm equal to c. It therefore converges against both eta_j and W_j eta_j. These observations give the ordinary term and the two residual terms in (7) with the printed signs.

For the logarithmic term, its support has ell_j>c, so ell_j=s. With r_j=lambda_j s,

    lambda_j ell_j Phi=f r_j t g(lambda_j t).

Its difference from f r_j s g(r_j) is bounded by a constant times lambda_j s: one term is r_j c times a bounded g, and the other is r_j Lip(g) lambda_j c s. The common rate bound controls the latter. Integrating proves (8); the ordinary part has r=0. The R_j contribution is also O(lambda_j integral s) and vanishes.

The order of limits is explicit and valid: j first with f,T fixed; then T tends to infinity using ordinary ell_+ integrability; then f+delta decreases to f if f can vanish. No claim of uniformity when T grows with j is made or needed.

For g(r)=(r-t)_+, the exact algebra

    r(r-t)_+=(r-t)_+^2+t(r-t)_+

gives (10). All terms retain their actual joint rate/normal/physical measure. The allowed class of g does not permit arbitrary interval indicators, so the source correctly refuses pointwise disintegration in r.

## 5. Exact calibration of that final limitation

At one fixed physical point and one fixed normal, take beta=1/2 and the abstract residual rate measures

    bhat=delta_0+delta_(1/4),
    ahat=(3/4)delta_0.

They have 0<=ahat<=bhat and rates in [0,beta]. For EVERY nonnegative nondecreasing g, hence for the entire allowed convex subclass,

    int g d ahat+int r g d bhat-beta int g d bhat
       =(g(0)-g(1/4))/4<=0.                         (B)

Thus all rate-weighted inequalities hold, including every hinge tail. Yet the low-rate load is 3/4, strictly greater than beta-r=1/2 there. The unweighted mass bound is an equality: a(total)+q(total)=3/4+1/4=beta b(total).

This is a residual-measure calibration only. It is not asserted to arise from an actual minimizing body or to satisfy the additional geometric flux identities. It shows exactly why the theorem's valid weighted inequalities cannot alone be relabeled as a pointwise cap-load estimate. No defect-exclusion conclusion is inferred.

The independent checker `supporting computation verify_scale_resolved_log_defect_audit_defect_transport.py` verifies the Hessian, truncation and tail identities and this rational calibration.
